do: Ensure every user interface component has a programmatically determinable name via accessible name computation
Expose roles for all interactive and region elements using native HTML semantics or ARIA roles
Ensure values of controls (e.g., inputs, sliders, lists) are programmatically available to assistive technologies
Use semantic HTML elements such as <button>, <input>, <a>, <select>, <textarea> for native support of name, role, and value
Use aria-label or aria-labelledby to provide accessible names when no visible label is present
Use aria-labelledby to reference existing visible text when multiple sources define a label
Keep name, role, and value in sync when components change state (e.g., toggled, expanded, selected)
Implement full ARIA widget pattern for custom components (e.g., combobox, slider, checkbox)
Ensure form fields are associated with labels via <label for> or aria-labelledby
Ensure each ARIA role has all required states and properties per ARIA specification
Use aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow for custom range widgets like sliders and spinbuttons
Use aria-pressed for toggle buttons and update its value appropriately on interaction
Use aria-checked on custom checkboxes or radio buttons and reflect changes in the DOM
Expose selected items in listboxes using aria-selected
Ensure aria-required, aria-invalid, and aria-describedby are used to convey form validation feedback
Use aria-hidden="true" only for purely decorative elements or hidden content that should not be read by assistive tech
Assign role="alert" or role="status" for live regions, and set aria-live for dynamic messaging
Ensure ARIA attributes like aria-labelledby or aria-describedby reference valid and existing IDs
For dialogs, use role="dialog" and point aria-labelledby to the dialog’s title element
Provide accessible names for SVG elements with role="img" via aria-label or aria-labelledby
Ensure that icon-only interactive elements (e.g., buttons, links) have a meaningful aria-label
Ensure that the accessible name matches or complements the visible label when both exist
Test custom components with screen readers to verify that name, role, and value are correctly exposed
Document accessible attribute patterns (name, role, value) in component library or design system
dont: Do not rely solely on visual labels without programmatic associations
Do not use ARIA roles that conflict with or override native HTML semantics unnecessarily
Do not leave aria-labelledby or aria-describedby referencing non-existent or duplicate IDs
Do not remove accessible name or role from elements through scripting or CSS
Do not use the title attribute as the only accessible name source
Do not hard-code aria-valuenow, aria-checked, or aria-pressed values without updating them on state change
Do not nest interactive roles (e.g., button inside link or vice versa)
Do not use ARIA roles on non-interactive elements when no interaction is expected
Do not use aria-* attributes that do not apply to the element’s role
Do not use custom widgets without providing proper roles and accessible names
Do not use multiple conflicting ARIA roles on the same element
Do not use aria-label and aria-labelledby together on the same element — choose one to avoid conflicts
Do not provide an accessible name that misrepresents the purpose or function of the element
Do not forget to localize accessible names for international audiences
Do not use role="presentation" or aria-hidden="true" on focusable or interactive elements
Do not use empty <label> elements without visible or programmatically associated content
Do not dynamically update control state (e.g., expanded, selected) without also updating the corresponding ARIA attribute
Do not use non-unique IDs for aria-labelledby or aria-describedby — this breaks the accessibility tree
Do not create custom controls without testing their name, role, and value with assistive technologies
Do not use placeholder text as a replacement for <label> — it disappears on focus and isn't a reliable accessible name
Do not use role="none" on meaningful content — it will remove it from the accessibility tree
Do not use aria-label on groups of elements when individual elements need distinct names
Do not forget to provide accessible names for elements used as buttons/controls inside SVG or Canvas
Do not create form controls that rely on visual grouping alone to imply their label or purpose
Do not override accessible name with JavaScript without updating visible label when they should be in sync
edge_cases: Custom dropdowns: Use role='combobox' with aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, and aria-activedescendant to convey state and control
Sliders: Use role='slider' with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, and optionally aria-valuetext for contextual value
Spinbuttons: Use role='spinbutton' with appropriate aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext for formatted numbers
Checkbox styled as toggle: Use role='checkbox' with aria-checked and ensure the label is announced
Menus and submenus: Use role='menu', role='menuitem' and support aria-haspopup and aria-expanded to expose relationships
Tree views: Use role='tree' and role='treeitem', with aria-expanded and aria-level to indicate nesting and state
Grids and tables: Use role='grid', with aria-rowindex, aria-colindex, and aria-selected on rows or cells as needed
SVG or canvas controls: Apply role='button' or other relevant roles and include aria-label or aria-labelledby
Dialogs: Use role='dialog' with aria-modal='true' and label the dialog via aria-labelledby or aria-label
Live regions: Use role='status' or aria-live='polite/assertive' to announce updates without stealing focus
Tab panels: Use role='tablist', role='tab', and role='tabpanel'; manage aria-selected and aria-labelledby correctly
Custom switch: Use role='switch' and aria-checked, ensure correct label for on/off states
Color pickers: Use role='listbox' or role='grid' and expose value using aria-valuetext
Custom rating controls: Represent as a group of buttons or role='slider' with accessible value and label
ARIA toolbar: Use role='toolbar' with grouped items and label the toolbar using aria-label or aria-labelledby
Graphical data points: Use role='img' with aria-label or aria-describedby linking to contextual info
Date pickers: Use role='dialog' for calendar and aria-selected for selected day
Hidden controls: Ensure hidden interactive elements are removed from accessibility tree or marked with aria-hidden
Custom widgets do not expose their role, state, or name to assistive technologies.
Dynamic components fail to announce changes in state such as expanded or collapsed panels.
Duplicate or missing roles create ambiguity in accessibility trees.
Automation can detect ARIA presence but not runtime synchronization between UI and AT output.
Interactive elements missing defined names or roles cannot be identified programmatically.
Dynamic content where roles and states are not updated appropriately.
techniques: ARIA1: Using aria-label to provide an accessible name
ARIA2: Using aria-labelledby to reference visible labels
ARIA3: Using aria-describedby to provide additional descriptions
ARIA4: Using valid ARIA roles like button, link, checkbox, radio, slider, spinbutton
ARIA5: Using state attributes like aria-checked, aria-selected, aria-expanded
ARIA6: Using value attributes like aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext
ARIA7: Using aria-live and aria-relevant for dynamic updates
H44: Using elements to associate text labels with form controls
H91: Using native HTML form controls and links appropriately
G108: Using markup features to expose the name and role, allow user-settable properties to be set, and notify changes
G135: Using accessibility API features to expose names and roles
G198: Providing a way for assistive technology users to determine what actions are available
axe_rules_hint: aria-attribute-name: Ensures only valid ARIA attributes are used
role-img-alt: Ensures role='img' elements have accessible names
aria-required-parent: Ensures required parent roles are present
aria-label: Ensures aria-label is present and non-empty when used
aria-labelledby: Ensures referenced IDs in aria-labelledby exist and are not empty
button-name: Ensures elements have accessible names
link-name: Ensures elements have accessible names
input-button-name: Ensures <input type='button'> elements have names
